name: pdk-medplum-durable-subscription-dispatch
instr:
# Goal

Rest-hook subscriptions can lose a committed FHIR change when Redis is unavailable or an API process stops after commit. Make delivery recoverable across API and worker processes without making successful FHIR writes dependent on Redis.

# Requirements

1. A committed `POST /fhir/R4/Patient`, `PUT /fhir/R4/Patient/{id}`, or `DELETE /fhir/R4/Patient/{id}` that matches an active `rest-hook` `Subscription` (`criteria: Patient`) reaches its HTTP endpoint. Deliver each matching change, including intermediate versions, in increasing version order per resource, with a distinct `X-Medplum-Delivery-Id` per subscription/change that stays the same on retries. Include the resource version in `X-Medplum-Version-Id` (for a delete, the new version the deletion creates).
2. FHIR writes return successfully while Redis is down for 20 seconds; all committed changes reach their receivers within 45 seconds of recovery. A write committed before an API process is killed must also be delivered after restart. Two APIs and two workers can run concurrently, including concurrent writes to the same resource, without duplicate acknowledged delivery IDs or reordered versions.
3. If a receiver returns 503 for 20 seconds and later returns 200, retry until acknowledged; begin the first retry within 10 seconds of the first failure.
